description:
FILED s473t5f (2026-09-14, Opus) from the round's companion legs.  Measured, not
inferred: every number below is a run on this box, and the A/B side is a
`git archive edd6dc78` extraction (scratch/s473t5f/basemain in that worktree).

THE FACT: the two `gv.t` files straddle the companion runner's 90 s default
clock, so their VERDICT is a function of machine load, not of the tree.

  t/uni/gv.t, --jobs 1, default --timeout 90:
    base (main edd6dc78): DIFF 74/85, DIFF, DIFF, then TIMEOUT, DIFF, DIFF,
                          TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT      -- 5 DIFF / 3 TIMEOUT of 8
    mine (s473t5f tip):   TIMEOUT, DIFF 75/84, TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT (</dev/null),
                          DIFF 75/84 (</dev/null), TIMEOUT  -- 2 DIFF / 4 TIMEOUT of 6
    The three DIFF runs on base all read 74/85; the two on mine both read 75/84.
    The first three base runs were taken at load ~2 and the TIMEOUTs at load
    7-9: LOAD is the variable.  Neither tree is stable.
  t/op/gv.t, same form:
    base: TIMEOUT 67/24, then DIFF 89/96.   mine: TIMEOUT 67/24.

WHAT IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE ROUND (and only this): uni/gv.t reads ONE ROW
BETTER when it finishes -- 74/85 -> 75/84.  Reproduced on a third tree,
`basecl` = main + ONLY the cl/ half of #1737 (its runtime differs from the
round's by the generation string alone, Pl/ untouched): 75/84.  The emission is
not involved -- `./pl2cl < t/uni/gv.t` is byte-identical between the round's
tree and main apart from the preamble paths and the gen stamp.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT, with the measurement:
  * the `runperl(prog => ...)` child at uni/gv.t:315 (a child SBCL under
    tools/pclperl-for-tests).  Extracted to scratch/s473t5f/gv-child.pl and
    timed ALONE: 0 s on the round's tree, 1 s on base.  Not the cost.
  * the runner's STDIN (the file does `readline $ary[0]` on a tied element
    holding *DATA, and ./runpcl stalls there on BOTH trees).  Re-run with
    `< /dev/null`: still 1 TIMEOUT of 2.  Not the cause under the runner.
  * a cold module cache from the round's generation bump: `basecl` carries
    main's generation (warm) and shows the same instability.

WHY NO TIMEOUT ALLOWANCE WAS REGISTERED.  baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv
promises a clock a file will finish inside.  The tail here is long -- one
uni/gv.t run on the round's tree did not finish inside 600 s, and one base run
did not finish inside 300 s -- so no number can be promised.  This is the same
reasoning s473t5f applied to uni/variables.t (#1750).  Registering 90->300 would
convert a visible TIMEOUT into an occasional invisible one.

WHY THE SNAPSHOT ROWS WERE NOT SPLICED.  Both rows in
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv are ALREADY stale against MAIN, not against this
round: uni/gv.t reads 59/29 there and main measures 74/85; op/gv.t reads 135/56
and main measures 89/96.  An unstable verdict is not a measurement, so neither
row was touched.  Whoever fixes the instability re-blesses both with a cause.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: uni/gv.t's 147 blessed fail rows are reported UNVERIFIED
on any run where it times out, and op/gv.t's rows likewise -- exactly the #176
hole (a file that times out contributes NO rows, so a regression inside it is
invisible).  A TIMEOUT can also lose the rows the child already printed: PCL's
TAP goes to a FILE, so it is block-buffered and flushed at exit; uni/gv.t's
timeouts read C 0/0 while op/gv.t's read C 67/24, the difference being whether
4 KB accumulated before the kill.

FIRST STEPS FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: (1) time the PCL side of uni/gv.t on an idle
box, at both trees, and find WHERE the seconds go (the file is 206 perl rows
and PCL produces 159 of them); it is a Target-A question as much as a harness
one.  (2) Decide whether the harness should flush TAP per row so a killed file
still contributes what it produced -- that would make the #176 hole shallower
for every timing-out file, not just these two.
subject: uni/gv.t and op/gv.t straddle the companion 90 s clock -- the verdict is a function of machine LOAD, both snapshot rows are stale against main, and a timed-out file loses its buffered TAP
